advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Gate genesis/TOFU on `keyring_epoch == 0` (never any key event), not on `not state['keys']`, so a revoke-all cannot re-open unsigned TOFU add.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/identity.py:261: `    is_genesis = not (state.get("keys") or [])`

process_key_event/_rederive_keyring_keys leave `state['keys']==[]` after revoking the last valid record: `if added <= epoch and (revoked is None or ... epoch < revoked)` (src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:48) excludes a record with `revoked_epoch == keyring_epoch-1`
AC (e165-377b-a8e3-49c9): 'Key add/rotate/revoke is refused unless signed by a currently-valid key of that identity'
`keyring_epoch` (a monotonic cursor, 0 iff no key event ever folded) is available and would distinguish true genesis from revoke-all, but the gate reads only `keys`
advisory.finding: `add_identity_key` treats any identity with no CURRENTLY-valid keys as genesis/TOFU (`is_genesis = not (state.get("keys") or [])`), so after all keys are revoked the next KEY_ADD is accepted WITHOUT a signature — re-opening trust-on-first-use takeover on an identity that previously held keys. This contradicts the ticket AC that key add/revoke must be signed by a currently-valid key.
scenarios: An identity's sole/last key is revoked (legitimately or by a compromised-then-revoked key), then an attacker with store-write access appends an unsigned KEY_ADD and takes over the identity.
advisory.suggested_fix: Compute genesis from the lifecycle cursor, e.g. `is_genesis = int(state.get('keyring_epoch') or 0) == 0`, so an identity that has ever held a key always requires a signed add even when its keyring is currently empty.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either wire `epoch_for_position` into a real caller with coverage, or drop it until needed.
evidence: search for `epoch_for_position` returns only its definition (authorship.py:159) and a docstring mention in tests/unit/test_identity_e165_heldout.py:159
tests/unit/test_identity_e165_heldout.py:166-168 asserts on `st["keyring_epoch"]`, never calling `epoch_for_position`
advisory.finding: `epoch_for_position` is unreachable dead code: no production caller invokes it and no test exercises it (the heldout test only names it in a docstring and asserts on `keyring_epoch`). It ships untested despite being the snapshot-aware epoch resolver.
scenarios: Future callers rely on epoch_for_position without any regression coverage for its snapshot base + pre-position counting logic.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Compare KEY-event positions using the shared integer comparator (`prefix_ts`/`event_sort_key`), not lexical string comparison of the position prefix.
evidence: src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:212: `        if _position_prefix(base) < event_position:`
src/rebar/reducer/_sort.py:24-25: `seg = os.path.basename(name).split("-", 1)[0]` / `return int(seg) if seg.isdigit() else -1` (integer compare is the single shared comparator)
src/rebar/_store/hlc.py:19-23: legacy 19-digit ns and HLC names are 'both plain integers; ordering compares them as integers' — string comparison 'only agrees while every name has the same width'
advisory.finding: `epoch_for_position` compares event positions LEXICALLY (`_position_prefix(base) < event_position`) for the HLC timestamp prefix, diverging from the canonical INTEGER comparator used everywhere else for event ordering (`reducer._sort.prefix_ts` / `event_sort_key`). The hlc module explicitly warns the prefix must be integer-compared across mixed digit widths; lexical compare agrees only while every timestamp has identical width.
scenarios: A store containing a shorter/longer timestamp prefix (or a future >19-digit HLC) would mis-count preceding KEY events, yielding a wrong epoch and a wrong epoch-scoped trust root.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drop the no-op `removesuffix(RETIRED_SUFFIX)` in epoch_for_position pass 2 (files are pre-filtered to active).
evidence: src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:181: listdir filter includes `and is_active_event(f)` (retired files excluded)

advisory.finding: In `epoch_for_position` pass 2, the file list is already filtered to active events via `is_active_event`, so `os.path.basename(path).removesuffix(RETIRED_SUFFIX)` never strips anything — dead handling that implies retired files are considered here when they are not.
scenarios: Reader assumes retired KEY events are scanned/handled here; they are silently filtered out earlier.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish 'never had a key' (true genesis) from 'all keys revoked' so an unsigned KEY_ADD is refused once an identity has ever held a key.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/identity.py:261: `is_genesis = not (state.get("keys") or [])`
src/rebar/_commands/identity.py:263-265: `if not is_genesis: _verify_keyop_signature(...)` — signature only required when keys is non-empty
src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:58-63: `_rederive_keyring_keys` sets `state["keys"] = keys_valid_at_epoch(keyring, epoch)`; when all records are revoked at/before the latest epoch this list is empty
src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:48: validity requires `revoked is None or epoch < revoked` — a fully-revoked keyring yields no valid keys

ABSENCE: held-out test file tests/unit/test_identity_e165_heldout.py revokes only the single genesis key but never asserts that a subsequent UNSIGNED add is refused; the all-keys-revoked genesis re-open case is untested
advisory.finding: Revoking (or letting expire) ALL of an identity's keys re-opens the trust-on-first-use path: add_identity_key computes `is_genesis = not (state.get('keys') or [])`, and state['keys'] is re-derived as keys_valid_at_epoch at the latest epoch, which is empty once every key is revoked. An identity that has had a full key lifecycle can therefore accept a NEW, UNSIGNED KEY_ADD, letting any party re-seed the keyring and take over the identity's authorship trust root without a signature from any previously-valid key.
scenarios: An operator revokes a compromised sole key intending to lock the identity; before a legitimate signed re-key, an attacker runs `rebar identity key add <id> <attacker_key>` with no --signature-file and succeeds, since the identity now reports zero valid keys.
A key with a revoked_epoch <= latest epoch leaves the identity keyless; any writer can then bootstrap an attacker-controlled key as 'genesis'.
advisory.suggested_fix: Base the genesis decision on whether the keyring has EVER had a record (e.g. `is_genesis = not (state.get('keyring') or [])` or `keyring_epoch == 0`), not on the currently-valid `keys` list. Once any key has existed, require a signature by a currently-valid key (or fail closed if none are valid).
